instructions.content: Run `pantheon-adr create [slug] -d "<description>"` to create a record from the Branch ADR template; with no slug the branch name supplies both the slug and the type.
A record's YAML frontmatter is the single source of truth for its status, author, tags, supersede links and status history. There is no index file to keep in step.
Records are identified by slug and stored as <slug>.md; there is no NNNN- number prefix and no next-number arithmetic.
Run `pantheon-adr check <slug>` before requesting review. The slug is required, and the record must score at least 80 of 100.
Never hand-edit `status:` in frontmatter. `review` and `update` append a timestamped history entry as they move the status; editing it directly skips the audit trail.

Supersede in two steps: create the replacement with `create`, then run `pantheon-adr update <old-slug> --superseded-by <new-slug>`, which also writes the reverse `supersedes` link. There is no `supersede` command.
Never rewrite an accepted record to change its decision; supersede it so the history is preserved.
The ADR directory resolves from `--dir` (after the subcommand), then ADR_DIR, then the default docs/adr. The default is a committed path on purpose.
Never rename or reorder the template headings; `check` scores sections by heading name, so renaming one drops its weight and caps the score.
Never leave `<!-- ... -->` placeholders in a finished record: any remaining comment forfeits 20 points and three or more cap the score at 70.
Always populate Options Considered with real alternatives and the reason each lost; a boilerplate filter scores filler text as if the section were empty.
Never record multiple unrelated decisions in one record; split them so each can be superseded independently.
Valid statuses are proposed, review-requested, accepted, deprecated and superseded. There is no rejected status.
`pantheon-adr index` regenerates index.md from the records' frontmatter. It is derived output: never hand-edit it.
Record an extracted decision's provenance in the frontmatter `related` list, not as a duplicate Source: bullet in the prose.
Run scripts/check-undocumented-decisions.sh to find planning documents with a decision that no record's `related` list points at.
